memory_lessons.applicability: Measured only for the supplied benchmark cases; this candidate changes only the CND exponential route and still requires controller validation.
memory_lessons.claim: The recorded guarded four-option SSE2 route retaining scalar transcendental calls was valid at 5.631 ms, while the guarded SSE2 polynomial log/exp route was valid at 2.662 ms; these results motivate testing a narrower approximation rather than assuming it will match either result.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the CND-only SSE2 exponential approximation separately over varied sizes and seeds, then compare correctness and time with the scalar baseline and full vector-math route.

proposal.hypothesis: The full SSE2 math route measured 2.662 ms and the SIMD arithmetic route retaining scalar transcendental calls measured 5.631 ms, versus the 7.529 ms scalar baseline. This candidate tests a narrower bottleneck: keep scalar logf, sqrtf, and discount expf calculations, but evaluate both CND exponentials and polynomials with guarded SSE2. It may offer a different accuracy/performance tradeoff; speed and tolerance compliance are unmeasured.

retained: Kept the scalar Black-Scholes routine intact as the unsupported-build, unsafe-range, and tail fallback.
Added an SSE2 four-option path that computes d1, d2, and discount values with scalar math while vectorizing the supplied CND polynomial and its exponential approximation.
Guarded the vector CND exponential to [-80, 0], falling back to the scalar routine for any four-option group outside that range.
Kept threading, the entrypoint contract, and compiler flags unchanged.
